title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.

questions.prompt: On a 1 : 10 000 orthophoto map a road is 6 cm long. What is its real length in metres?
Which gradient is steepest?
When calculating gradient, VI and HE must be in the same unit.
On a 1 : 50 000 map, the horizontal distance between two points is 3 cm and the height difference is 75 m. Calculate the average gradient.
Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Difference in height between two points
Angle between true north and magnetic north

questions.prompt: A learner calculated the area of a 4 cm × 2 cm block on a 1 : 50 000 map as 8 × 0,5 = 4 km². Explain the mistake and give the correct answer.
questions.memo:
✓ Each side must be converted to km before multiplying (1)
✓ 2 km × 1 km = 2 km² (1)

questions.prompt: The standard scale of a South African topographic map is…
The standard scale of an orthophoto map is…
An orthophoto map is a larger scale than a topographic map.
V-shaped contours pointing towards higher ground show a…
What is the contour interval on a South African orthophoto map?
Match each landform to its contour pattern.

pairs.right: Wide flat top with steep sides
Long line of contours very close together

questions.prompt: How many seconds are in one minute of latitude?
Give TWO differences between a topographic map and an orthophoto map.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): scale; area shown; detail; photograph vs symbols; contour interval 20 m vs 5 m

questions.prompt: What does GIS stand for?
The number of beds in a hospital is an example of…
What is collecting information about the Earth from satellites called?
A high-resolution image shows more detail than a low-resolution image.
What are layers in a GIS and why are they useful?
questions.memo:
✓ Separate sets of data (e.g. roads, rivers, buildings) stored one above another (1)
✓ They can be overlaid or switched off to compare and see relationships (1)

questions.prompt: Explain what a buffer is, with an example.
questions.memo:
✓ A zone of a set distance drawn around a feature (1)
✓ e.g. 100 m along a river where no building is allowed / 1 km around a factory (1)

questions.prompt: Name FOUR components of a GIS.
questions.memo: ✓✓ Any four (½ each, round up): hardware, software, data, people, methods

questions.prompt: Which resource is renewable?
Which sector uses the most water in South Africa?
About what percentage of South Africa's electricity comes from coal?
Name the scheme that transfers water from Lesotho to Gauteng.
Match each action to one of the three Rs.

pairs.left: Taking a shopping bag to the shop again and again
Turning old bottles into new glass

questions.prompt: South Africa's average rainfall is higher than the world average.
Explain how overgrazing leads to soil erosion.
questions.memo:
✓ Too many animals eat the grass faster than it can regrow, leaving bare ground (1)
✓ Without plant cover and roots, rain and wind wash or blow the soil away (1)

questions.prompt: Why is it important to involve local communities in conservation?
questions.memo:
✓ They benefit from jobs and income, e.g. eco-tourism (1)
✓ so they have a reason to protect the resources instead of over-using them (1)
